paper_metadata.title: Alterations of connectivity patterns in functional brain networks in patients with mild traumatic brain injury: A longitudinal resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear definition of the target population (mTBI) using established ACRM criteria and describes the recruitment process from a tertiary center. Baseline characteristics are well-documented and compared with a matched control group.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Sixty-five adult patients with mTBI were originally recruited prospectively from a tertiary health-care centre in the city of Delhi
items.reasoning: The source (tertiary center) and the nature of the population (adult mTBI) are clearly stated.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: recruited prospectively from a tertiary health-care centre... All participants had sustained closed-head TBI through road traffic accidents
items.reasoning: Prospective recruitment from a specific clinical setting is described.

items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: While the timing relative to injury is mentioned (within 7 days), the calendar dates of the recruitment period are not provided.

items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The definition of mTBI was taken as per the criteria laid down by the American Congress of Rehabilitation Medicine... Exclusion criteria were the presence of pre-existing neurological/psychiatric disorders, drug abuse, polytrauma, prior history of TBI
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical criteria (ACRM) and specific exclusion factors are listed.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a very high rate of attrition for the longitudinal component (60 patients at baseline vs 21 at 6 months). The study does not provide a comparison of baseline characteristics between those who completed the follow-up and those who dropped out, creating a high risk of attrition bias.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the 60 patients who were initially assessed, 25 reported for a repeat study at 6 months. Of these, four patients had to be excluded... A detailed follow-up study could be performed 6 months after injury on 21 patients.
items.reasoning: Only 35% (21/60) of the original sample completed the follow-up, which is below the standard threshold for low risk.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (mTBI status) is well-defined by clinical standards and the measurement tool (3T MRI) is a high-quality, objective instrument with standardized protocols.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The definition of mTBI was taken as per the criteria laid down by the American Congress of Rehabilitation Medicine.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: MRI data were collected on a Siemens Skyra 3.0 T scanner... The structural brain MR images... were examined by an experienced neuroradiologist.
items.reasoning: 3T MRI is an objective, reliable tool, and scans were reviewed by a specialist.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The de-noised data were decomposed into a set of 20 independent components by running MELODIC again.
items.reasoning: Standard ICA decomposition methods were used rather than arbitrary data-driven cut-points for the PF.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The same imaging protocol was repeated for patients 6 months after injury. Controls had only one MRI investigation (with an identical protocol as that of patients).
items.reasoning: Consistency in measurement across groups and time points is explicitly stated.

items.evidence_snippet: Of the 65 cases, five patients had a suboptimal MRI scan. A total of 60 patients were thus finally included
items.reasoning: The vast majority of recruited patients provided usable baseline PF data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes (PCS symptoms and neurocognitive scores) were measured using validated, standardized instruments (RPSQ and PGIBBD) applied consistently to all participants.

items.evidence_snippet: presence and severity of post-concussion symptoms were assessed by the Rivermead Post-Concussion Symptoms Questionnaire (RPSQ)... All patients who reported 6 months after injury were assessed using the Postgraduate Institute Battery of Brain Dysfunction (PGIBBD)

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses sophisticated and appropriate statistical methods for fMRI (ICA, dual regression, permutation testing) and accounts for multiple comparisons. The reporting of results is comprehensive and aligns with the stated aims.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: The fMRI data were preprocessed using the FMRI Expert Analysis Tool (FEAT)... dual regression technique was used for between-group analysis
items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline is described in detail.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: A general linear model was used to generate a multi-subject design matrix for two groups
items.reasoning: The use of GLM and ICA is standard for this type of neuroimaging study.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: FSL randomised non-parametric permutation testing with 10,000 permutations... Threshold-free cluster enhancement was used to control for multiple comparisons
items.reasoning: Robust non-parametric methods were used to handle the multiple comparisons problem inherent in fMRI.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 12 components were identified as RSNs... No significant differences between mTBI and control subjects were found in the intrinsic connectivity of the other visualised networks.
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant findings across all identified networks.
